newsitem.title: USA: Lakeland sees growth from clean-up bill.
newsitem.headline: Lakeland sees growth from clean-up bill.

text.p: Lakeland Industries Inc said growth in the protective clothing market could accelerate if Congress passed pending legislation to increase federal government funds to clean up Super Fund toxic waste sites.

"If Congress passes the bill, it'll probably take about a year before the funds actually hit the contractors," said Christopher Ryan, Lakeland's executive vice-president of finance. "It's the government that's been dragging its feet; the petrochemical companies and the insurance companies already have reserved $15 billion each."

For the three-month fiscal period ended April 30, the company's net sales increased 14 percent to about $12.0 million, versus $10.5 million in the first quarter of 1996. Net income rose 12.7 percent to $470,692 ($0.18 per share), compared with $417,825 ($0.16 per share) for the same period last year.

The manufacturer and distributor of disposable and re-usable protective work clothing gained several new industrial accounts in its first quarter, said Lakeland's chief executive Raymond Smith in a statement. He added the company expanded production capacity outside the U.S.
